metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is low, model tends to underreact — correct by adding 2–5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40% in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to align with historical mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.5) and forecast is high, model often overestimates — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence bias.
- When true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day forecast, check if sentiment shifted sharply — if yes, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment turns bullish, add 3–5% to forecast).
- Model consistently underestimates true values in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 3–7% for first 5 days to account for lag.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model often fails to anticipate recovery — add 2–5% to forecast in 8–15 day window to capture sentiment reversal.
